belief: Everyone I love eventually betrays me.
origins: Repeated hurt by parents, partners, friends, or church can form a pattern: love ends in betrayal. We may expect it, pull away early, or test people until they fail. Sometimes we choose people who repeat the pattern, and the belief is then confirmed.
teaches: Scripture is honest about betrayal. The psalmist writes, “It is not an enemy who insults me… But it is you, a man like myself, my companion and close friend,” and “Even my close friend whom I trusted… has lifted up his heel against me.” Isaiah says of the Messiah, “He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief.” Jesus was betrayed by Judas and denied by Peter. Yet after Peter’s failure, Jesus restored him. And God promises, “Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you.” You are not alone in betrayal, and betrayal is not the final word.
self_statements: It is only a matter of time.
errors: Treating repeated hurt as a universal rule.
Remembering betrayals and forgetting loyal people.
Pulling away or testing people and causing the very break I fear.
questions: Who has betrayed me, and what do these experiences have in common?
Who has stayed loyal to me?
What patterns in my choices or expectations might I need to examine?
What does it mean that Jesus was betrayed too?
How did Jesus respond to Peter after his failure?
What would healthy trust look like?
truth: I have been betrayed, and the pain is real. But not everyone betrays, and I am not alone. Jesus knows betrayal and promises never to leave me. I can heal, examine my patterns, and learn to trust wisely.
hw_truths: God will never leave me or forsake me.
Betrayal is not the last word.
I can choose and trust wisely.
log: Each week, name one person who has been loyal and one way you showed appreciation.
actions: Write names of people who have stayed with you.
With a counselor, examine the common threads in your relationships.
prayer: Lord Jesus, You know what betrayal feels like. Heal my wounds, help me see the faithful people around me, and teach me to love and trust wisely. Thank You that You never leave. Amen.
hw_questions: What does healthy trust look like?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God said, ‘Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you.’”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Everyone I love eventually betrays me.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
